messages:
michael: Heads up — noticed a regression in the Qwen2.5 nightly perf run with our multilingual suite. p99 jumped from ~52ms to ~78ms for streaming token paths on seq=1024, batch=1. Repro on dedicated node.

jia: can you paste the bench command + the raw numbers?

michael: repro: `./bench --model qwen2.5 --seq 1024 --batch 1 --stream --tokenizer qwen_v2`
results: baseline(2025-11-02) p50=39ms p99=52ms mean=41ms; current p50=53ms p99=78ms mean=57ms; throughput -22%.

olga: I pulled kernel-selection logs for that run — looks like several middle layers (8..11) are picking `attn_fallback_generic` instead of `attn_optimized` when the token sequence contains high fraction of CJK tokens. That explains the CPU->GPU kernel shift.

len: paste kernel-selection trace?

perf-bot: kernel-selection: layer_7 kernel=attn_optimized (ok) layer_8 kernel=attn_fallback_generic (reason=unsupported_stride) layer_9 kernel=attn_fallback_generic (reason=kv_head_mismatch) layer_10 kernel=attn_optimized

jia: profiler breakdown (GPU kernel time):
```
attn_optimized: 42.3%
attn_generic: 28.7%
kv_cache_copy: 12.6%
other: 16.4%
```

olga: aside — KV cache churn observed. For multilingual inputs, every ~8th token triggers a cache invalidation path (we see cache_write_size reset). Suspect head/kv layout mismatch after tokenization-normalization changes.

len: are head dims changing per head? Qwen2.5 uses head_dim=64 normally. Any per-head variance would be a red flag.

michael: example tokenization case that triggers it:
```
python repro_tokenize.py --text "这是一个测试。Hello world!" --tokenizer qwen_v2
# tokens len=127 -> after normalization becomes 205 (subword markers inserted)
```

jia: interesting — the rope_scale heuristic in runtime computes sin/cos stride with assumption that token positions are contiguous and < 4096. If tokenizer emits lots of subword markers or special BOS/SEP repeats, we push effective seq shapes into an unexpected packing branch and kernel selector rejects optimized kernel due to stride/pos mismatch.

olga: I forced `RW_KERNEL_FORCE=attn_optimized` and reran microbench — p99 recovered to ~54ms but hit correctness blips on long-span attention (small token corruption observed in a tiny subset). So forcing kernel masks the perf issue but breaks positional semantics -> indicates positional encoding handling differs between kernels (ALiBi vs RoPE variant expectations).

perf-bot: kv_debug snapshot (when enabled): head0_dim=64 expected=64 head7_dim=32 expected=64 -> mismatch detected at layer_10 -> invalidating kv cache for remainder of sequence.

len: head7_dim=32? that smells like packing/quantization artifact — perhaps int8 packing truncated last 32 dims for some fused linear layouts. We had a similar bug months ago where weight packing used different padding for multilingual vocab offsets.

jia: other datapoints: batching heuristics show that when we pack heterogeneous seq lengths the runtime does repeated reselect/compile of kernels across batch elements which kills throughput. The multilingual tokenizer has much higher variance in token lengths, so our batching thresholds should avoid per-batch recompile.

michael: exact failure log for the corrupted token case: `pos_encode_mismatch: expected_rope_scale=1.0 got=0.875; fallback=true`. Looks like rope_scale table computed from seq_len distribution was different between optimized and generic paths.

olga: proposed short-term mitigations:
- add an invariant check in kernel selector: if head_dim mismatch -> do not silently invalidate KV, log and skip fallback
- relax rope_scale heuristic for Qwen2.5 (disable auto-scaling)
- tighten tokenizer normalization so we avoid inserting excessive subword markers for multilingual short inputs

len: long-term: audit quantized packing path (int8) for per-head padding, add unit test for head_dim consistency across fused ops; add tokenization fuzz tests with high variance languages (zh, ja, th, ar, ru) to perf suite.

jia: action items assigned:
1) michael - run multilingual token fuzz (100k examples) and collect kernel-selection stats, post by EOD (1795001678).
2) olga - try a patched attn_optimized that preserves positional output semantics (small guard) and run correctness+perf microbench.
3) len - instrument packing code with asserts for head_dim and kv buffer length, run static analyzer.
4) infra - temporarily disable rope_scale autoscaling for qwen2.5 production variant until root cause identified.

michael: I'll start the fuzz run now, enabling `RW_KV_DEBUG=1` and `RW_KERNEL_LOG=1`. Will share outputs here. If customers report visible corruption, we'll escalate to incident channel. :mag:

olga: also verifying whether ALiBi fallbacks exist in the optimized kernel path — differences in how we offset positions could be the root cause.

perf-bot: note: repro harness link -> https://ci.redwood.ai/perf/runs/1795001111 (contains traces, kernels, kv dumps)

michael: thanks all — will update.
